# Bluesight Prototypes — Static Site

This repo auto-generates a browsable site of all prototype files using GitHub Pages. Every push to `main` triggers a rebuild and redeploy.

## How it works

- **`build.py`** copies the repo into a `_site/` directory, then writes an `index.html` listing into every directory inside `_site/` (with a few exceptions — see below).
- It also writes a single **`_search-index.json`** at the root of `_site/` that powers global search.
- **`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`** runs the build on every push to `main` and deploys the contents of `_site/` to GitHub Pages.
- Your source tree is **never modified**. The build writes only into `_site/`.

## The three things a folder can be

The build decides what to do with each folder by what's inside it:

| Folder contains | Result | Visiting `/folder/` shows |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `landing.html` | **Wrapped landing.** Generated listing with the sidebar; `landing.html` auto-loads in the iframe. Other files in the folder are listed in the sidebar; `landing.html` is hidden. | Sidebar + your page in the iframe |
| `index.html` (user-provided) | **Bare landing.** Build leaves your file alone and generates no listing for this folder. | Your page, full-bleed, no sidebar |
| Neither | **Folder browser.** Generated listing with the sidebar; iframe is empty until a file is clicked. | Sidebar + empty viewer |

A folder containing **both** `index.html` and `landing.html` is an authoring error — the build will exit with a message naming the folder.

## One-time setup

1. Push these three files to your repo's `main` branch:
   - `build.py`
   - `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
   - This `README.md` (optional)

2. In your GitHub repo settings, enable Pages:
   - Settings → Pages → **Source: GitHub Actions**

3. Add `_site/` to your `.gitignore`:
   ```
   _site/
   ```

4. Push any commit to trigger the first build. After ~1 minute, your site is live at `https://<username>.github.io/<repo>/`.

## Adding prototypes

For most prototypes, you want them wrapped in the sidebar. Drop your prototype into a folder as `landing.html` and commit:

```
my-repo/
├── build.py
├── notes.md             (rendered at the top of the root sidebar)
├── login-flow/
│   ├── landing.html        ← your prototype, wrapped in sidebar at /login-flow/
│   └── styles.css
└── dashboard/
    └── landing.html        ← another prototype
```

If your prototype is exported from a tool that names the entry file `index.html`, just rename it to `landing.html` after copying it in.

## Adding bare landing pages

If you want a folder to be its own thing — a custom landing page with no sidebar — name the file `index.html` instead. The build will leave it alone:

```
my-repo/
└── product-overview/
    ├── index.html          ← served bare at /product-overview/
    ├── styles.css
    └── hero.png
```

Bare folders aren't reachable through the sidebar's file list (there's no listing to render), but the **parent** folder's listing still links to them, and they're findable in global search by folder name.

## Adding sidebar notes

Drop a `notes.md` (any case) into any folder that has a generated listing. Its rendered Markdown shows above the file list when you're in that folder. Markdown supports headings, bold, italic, lists, links, code, blockquotes, and inline images. Relative links resolve against the folder. (Notes in bare-landing folders are ignored — the user's `index.html` is the whole page.)

`README.md` files (any case) are hidden from listings by convention but not rendered as sidebar content — that's `notes.md`'s job. If you want sidebar content at the root of your site, create a `notes.md` at the repo root.

## Customizing

Open `build.py` and edit the `CONFIG` constants:

- **`TITLE`** — sidebar title (default: "Bluesight Prototypes")
- **`OUTPUT_DIR`** — where the build writes (default: `_site`)
- **`LANDING_FILENAME`** — the filename that triggers a wrapped landing (default: `landing.html`)
- **`EXCLUDE_NAMES`** — files/folders hidden from listings and search
- **`COPY_SKIP_NAMES`** — files/folders never copied into `_site/` at all
- **`EXCLUDE_PREFIXES`** — name prefixes to skip (default: `(".",)` for dotfiles)
- **`IFRAME_EXTS`** — extensions that load in the iframe viewer
- **`DEFAULT_FILES`** — auto-load these in the iframe when entering a folder

## Local preview

```bash
python3 build.py
python3 -m http.server -d _site 8000
```

Then open <http://localhost:8000>.

## Migration notes

If you're upgrading an existing repo:

- **From an in-place build** (older versions wrote `index.html` listings into source). The build detects committed listings via a `<!-- generated by build.py -->` marker, skips them in the copy, and prints them as a one-time cleanup warning. Run the build, delete the listed files from git, commit.
- **From the `prototype.html` convention** (intermediate version). Each existing prototype folder has an `index.html` that was being renamed at build time. With the new rules, those are now treated as **bare** landings — the sidebar disappears around them. To get the sidebar back, rename each prototype `index.html` → `landing.html`. The build prints a count of bare landings on every run as a reminder.

## Caveats vs. the PHP version

- **Listings update on push, not in real time.** Files added without going through git won't appear until the next build.
- **No `?p=` URL parameters.** Each folder has its own page (`/folder/`). Bookmarks still work, just with cleaner URLs.
- **Search has the same behavior** but loads from a pre-built JSON file instead of querying the server.
